subject: argument matching: consistency vs. special cases

messages.author: 2d475b13e63c8cd2
messages.subject: argument matching: consistency vs. special cases
parts:
Hi,

I never rely on positional arguments for anything serious, but the following got me thinking:

reg_fn_sq <- function(x) (x - .5)^2
ggplot(data.frame(x = seq(0, 1, by = .1)), aes(x)) + stat_function(reg_fn_sq)

reg_fn_sq is matched to the 'mapping' above, because mapping is the first argument to stat_function. I imagine that the reason that mapping is the first argument is because mapping is the first argument to many geoms and stats. I respect consistency but it seems a little strange because I don't think many people are going to override the general mapping very often. But everyone who uses stat_function will need to give it a function argument. Most of the help examples are just passing only the function argument, sometimes with a color or argument list.

For the sake of argument, I want to take the position that positional matching should be encouraged and have sensible defaults for the special case where the function is called with one argument. Also for the sake of argument, I want to say that this should take precedence over consistency. Why? Because the consistency or ordering argument names only comes into play when users rely on positional arguments for multiple arguments, which should not be encouraged.

As you can see by my two "for the sake of argument" statements, I'm not yet convinced by my reasoning. Just curious.

Any thoughts on this?

Best,

Scott
